title: India-Pakistan DGMOs Hold Hotline Talks — Both Sides Commit to No Firing, Discuss Forward Troop Reductions
detail: India's Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai and Pakistan's Maj Gen Kashif Abdullah held a round of military hotline talks on May 12, 2026, reviewing implementation of the ceasefire understanding from May 2025. Both sides committed to maintaining no firing and no aggressive action, and agreed to consider measures aimed at reducing border tensions including possible forward troop reductions. The talks were held at 17:00 (originally scheduled for 12:00) and represent one of the rare direct military-to-military contacts maintained since the Operation Sindoor / Marka-e-Haq ceasefire. Despite the dialogue at the military level, the broader diplomatic bilateral freeze remains fully intact: no ambassadors exchanged, mutual airspace closure extended through May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all direct trade halted.

media.caption: India and Pakistan DGMOs hold hotline talks on May 12, 2026, committing to no-firing and discussing forward troop reductions

title: Indian Air Defences Intercept Suspected Pakistani Drones in Samba, Rajouri, Poonch — Small-Scale UAV Incursions Along Border
detail: Indian air defences intercepted a small number of suspected Pakistani drones in the Samba sector along the India-Pakistan International Border in Jammu division on the evening of May 12, 2026. Army sources confirmed the drones were engaged and described 'no cause for alarm.' Drone sightings were also reported in Rajouri and Poonch sectors along the Line of Control. The incidents are consistent with a pattern of low-altitude UAV intrusions from the Pakistan side that have intensified since the May 2025 ceasefire; Indian security forces have deployed dedicated counter-drone systems across border districts in Jammu following Operation Sindoor. No casualties were reported. The drone intercept occurred on the same day as DGMO-level hotline talks, underscoring the tension between ongoing military dialogue and continued border incidents.

media.caption: Indian air defences intercept suspected Pakistani drones in Samba sector along the International Border on May 12, 2026

title: India MEA Issues Sharp Rebuke to China Over Operation Sindoor Technical Support to Pakistan
detail: India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a sharp statement on May 12, 2026 warning that countries which 'consider themselves responsible must reflect on the consequences of supporting actions linked to terrorist infrastructure' — a direct message aimed at China for providing technical assistance to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The rebuke came after Indian forces recovered an intact Chinese-origin PL-15 BVR (Beyond Visual Range) air-to-air missile during the conflict, which Indian officials cited as evidence of advanced Chinese weapons being used by Pakistan's air force against India. The MEA statement signalled that India views China's arms and technical support to Pakistan as enabling Pakistani military aggression, and framed this as relevant to China's global standing as a 'responsible' power. India has consistently objected to Chinese military technology transfers to Pakistan, including advanced fighter jets, missiles, and electronic warfare systems, throughout the post-Sindoor period.

media.caption: India MEA rebukes China over technical support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor — 'responsible countries must reflect on consequences'

title: Pakistan National Assembly Unanimously Passes Resolution Praising Armed Forces on Marka-e-Haq Anniversary
detail: Pakistan's National Assembly passed a unanimous resolution on May 11–12, 2026 praising the armed forces on the first anniversary of the Marka-e-Haq operation against India. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar moved the resolution; Speaker Ayaz Sadiq presided. The resolution was the legislative capstone of a week-long national commemoration campaign (May 5–12) that included a Corps Commanders' Conference, official book launch, DG ISPR press conference, anniversary documentary, and national military ceremonies. Speaker Sadiq hailed Pakistan's 'historic victory' in the operation. Opposition members briefly interrupted the session to protest rising utility prices, but the resolution passed unanimously. The parliamentary endorsement formalizes the Pakistani state's legislative ratification of the official victory narrative from Marka-e-Haq and its framing as a battle of ideologies.

media.caption: Pakistan National Assembly unanimously passes resolution honouring armed forces on first anniversary of Marka-e-Haq
